body.definition: Admissibility of a lagged SSOE model decided in exact rational arithmetic with certified root enclosures (independent/oracle.py, python-flint 0.9.0), written from the claimset definitions without the prototype: each float of F, g, w is converted exactly to a rational; D = F - g w'; theta(B) = det(I - D L(B)) and phi(B) = det(I - F L(B)), L(B) = diag(B^{l_1}, ..., B^{l_k}), by fraction-free (Bareiss) elimination over Q[B]; G = gcd(theta, phi) exactly and theta_G = theta / G (C17: its roots are the reciprocals of the reachable and observable modes); C = the product of the cyclotomic polynomials Phi_n, n dividing a lag, each removed while it divides both theta and phi (D6 in exact arithmetic), theta_C = theta / C; R = G / C. The modes are lambda = 1/B over the roots B of a polynomial, enclosed by Arb balls of 128 bits (raised to 512 and 2048 while a modulus ball contains 1); a polynomial is admissible when every |lambda| < 1 is certified, inadmissible when some |lambda| > 1 is certified or every ambiguous root is proved to be a root of unity exp(2 pi i k/n) with Phi_n dividing the polynomial exactly (|lambda| = 1), and undecided otherwise. The largest mode modulus is the max over the roots, with certified bounds.

The largest modulus among the eigenvalues lambda of the expanded discount matrix for which the smallest singular values of [lambda I - D~; w~'] and [lambda I - D~, g~] both exceed 1e-7 (||D~||_2 + ||g~|| + ||w~||), computed with numpy by the prototype (pbh_max, claimset D5); the model forgets its initial states when it is below 1.

body.term: prototype check of the whole model
body.definition: The numpy prototype of the check of the whole model (claimset D6, D10): theta and phi by inverse DFT, division by every Phi_n, n dividing a lag, while the remainder is at most 1e-9 times the sum of absolute coefficients, and the largest mode modulus 1/min|B| over numpy roots of the cancelled MA polynomial (max_lambda_cancelled); admissible when below 1.

The Levinson-Durbin step-down (Schur-Cohn) recursion on the prototype's cancelled MA polynomial 1 + c_1 B + ... + c_n B^n: for j = n, ..., 1, kappa_j = c_j and c_i <- (c_i - kappa_j c_{j-i}) / (1 - kappa_j^2); passes (admissible) when every |kappa_j| < 1 (claimset D7; stepdown_admissible).

body.term: bisection for the largest root modulus
body.definition: Bisection on r over the step-down test applied to theta*(B/r), to a width of 1e-10, giving the largest mode modulus where the root-based value exceeds 1 (claimset D11; bisection_max_lambda).
Every eigenvalue of every diagonal block of D, one block per unique lag, has modulus below 1 (claimset D4; per_lag_max, accepted when below 1).

body.term: models of the planned tests PL1-PL6 and the examples of RN2
body.definition: The models exported by AC4 with the prototype's values (export_models.py, which draws them as confirm.py and cpp_check.py do): RN57 (set perlag: 3042 ETS(A,N,A) grid models and 200 GUM with lags (1, 12), PL1 and PL2), RN58 (set cancel: the 500 models of PL3), RN59 (set stepdown: the 575 models of PL4 and PL5, theta of degree up to 535), RN60 (set cpp: the 800 models of PL6) and RN61 (set examples: the two models of C10 and C11); 5119 models in all.

Each model's admissibility decision and largest mode modulus by a method of the study and by the exact oracle on the same model: the number of models whose decisions differ, and the largest absolute difference of the modulus on the models both find inadmissible. The PBH reference is compared with theta_G (the exact gcd), the prototype's cancellation, step-down test and bisection with theta_C (the exact cyclotomic cancellation). Models the oracle leaves undecided, and models whose certified largest modulus (theta_G or theta_C) lies within 1e-8 of 1, are left out and counted (the band of the claimset's design D26, with the oracle as reference).
Whether a method accepts a model as admissible (decaying weights: every reachable and observable mode with |lambda| < 1); compared as the number of models on which two methods differ.

The largest |lambda| of the modes that decide admissibility: the PBH reference value, 1/min|B| over the roots of the cancelled MA polynomial, or the oracle's certified value; a model is admissible when it is below 1.

body.term: shared factor with a root in the closed unit disc that is not cyclotomic
body.definition: Whether R = gcd(theta, phi) / C, the factor shared by theta and phi after removing the cyclotomic polynomials Phi_n (n dividing a lag) at the multiplicity they divide both, has a root in |B| <= 1, certified by the exact oracle; counted over models (claimset C19 says never).

body.design: One run of independent/oracle.py (commit dc74fc0c, python-flint 0.9.0, 4 worker processes) on the five files RN57/models.json (perlag), RN58/models.json (cancel), RN59/models.json (stepdown), RN60/models.json (cpp) and RN61/models.json (examples): for each of the 5119 models the exact oracle computes theta, phi, their exact gcd G, the exact cyclotomic cancellation C (Phi_n, n dividing a lag, at the multiplicity dividing both) and R = G / C, and certified enclosures of the modes of theta_G = theta / G, theta_C = theta / C and R (Arb balls of 128 bits, raised to 512 and 2048 bits while a modulus ball contains 1; an ambiguous root counts as on the unit circle only when proved a root of unity whose Phi_n divides the polynomial). Compared with the prototype's values stored in the files: pbh_max (PBH reference) against theta_G; max_lambda_cancelled, stepdown_admissible and bisection_max_lambda against theta_C; per_lag_max with theta_G for the counts of C1 and C2. The oracle was checked beforehand only on models of other seeds (AC5.RN2, AC5.RN6, AC5.RN7) and on hand-checkable models (test_oracle.py).
body.analysis: Per set and over all sets: models given, failed, undecided and within the edge band (excluded and counted); admissibility decisions that differ (PBH reference: pbh_max < 1 against theta_G certified admissible; prototype: max_lambda_cancelled < 1 and stepdown_admissible against theta_C certified admissible) and the largest absolute difference of the largest mode modulus (midpoint of the certified bounds) on the models both find inadmissible; for the bisection, the largest absolute difference on every model with a bisection value; the models whose R has a root in |B| <= 1 (certified) or could not be located; for set perlag by family, the models with per_lag_max < 1 whose oracle modulus exceeds 1 + 1e-8 and the models with per_lag_max >= 1 whose oracle modulus is below 1 - 1e-8. Also reported, not used by the rules: the models whose exact cancelled degree differs from the prototype's degree_theta_cancelled, models with a shared non-cyclotomic factor whose roots all lie outside the unit disc, roots proved on the unit circle, maximum degrees, times.
body.new_data: The exact oracle has never been run on these models: its exploratory runs used models of other seeds (stepdown seed 11, cancel seed 12, cpp seed 13, and only the GUM models of perlag seed 14; the fixed ETS(A,N,A) grid and the two examples were never given to it). The hypotheses are a priori: they restate the claimset's claims C1-C4, C14, C16, C19 with the oracle in place of the references.

body.rationale: Rule of AC5.PL1 for AC5.H1: neither rule is met. No decision differs (mp = 0, mc = 0) and the moduli agree (dp = 4.66e-15, dc = 5.20e-10, both <= tol_a = 1e-6), so the not-supported rule fails; but the edge exclusion left out 81 of 5119 models (und = 0), more than max_excluded_share * n = 51.19, so the supported rule fails too. The excluded models are 78 ETS(A,N,A) grid models of set perlag (AC5.RS152) and 3 models of set cpp (AC5.RS216) whose certified largest modulus lies within 1e-8 of 1; the cap was set before the run without knowing how many grid models lie on the boundary.

Rule of AC5.PL1 for AC5.H2: on the 575 stepdown models (fs = 0, us = 0, es = 0) the step-down decisions differ from the exact oracle on ms = 0 models, the root-based largest modulus differs by at most ds = 6.59e-12 and the bisection value by at most db = 5.74e-11 (nb = 198 models), all <= tol_b = 1e-8.
Rule of AC5.PL1 for AC5.H3: fail = 0, nu = 0 and nc = 0: on none of the 5119 models does gcd(theta, phi) / C have a root in |B| <= 1.
Rule of AC5.PL1 for AC5.H4: fp = up = 0 and, with the exact oracle in place of the PBH reference, eb = 1482, er = 0, gb = 10, gr = 1, the counts of C1 and C2.

body.text: AC5.H1 is inconclusive only through its cap on exclusions: the edge band left out 81 of 5119 models (AC5.RS253), above the cap of 1% (51.19) fixed in AC5.PL1, with no model undecided (AC5.RS252) and no differing decision or modulus difference beyond 5.2e-10 on the 5038 compared (AC5.RS254, RS259, RS260, RS265, RS266). The breakdown (AC5.RN9): the 78 excluded models of set perlag are all ETS(A,N,A) grid models with alpha + gamma = 2 within 1e-12 (AC5.RS273, RS278), on the boundary of admissibility: their certified largest modulus is within 4.4e-16 of 1 (AC5.RS274); 2 of them (alpha = gamma = 1, m = 4 and 12) have roots proved to lie exactly on the unit circle (AC5.RS275), the others have float parameters a rounding off the line. On 6 of the 78 the PBH reference's decision (pbh_max < 1) differs from the exact oracle's (AC5.RS276), with moduli within 2.4e-15 (AC5.RS277): their decision is set by rounding. The 3 excluded models of set cpp are ETS models with seasonal lags from {24, 168, 365} whose certified modulus lies between 1 - 6.9e-9 and 1 (AC5.RS287, RS288); the prototype decides them as the oracle does, within 3.7e-14 (AC5.RS290, RS291). So the statement that none of the exported sets has a model within 1e-8 of 1 does not hold for sets perlag and cpp; the counts of C1 (E1) are unaffected because they apply the same band (AC5.H4 supported, AC5.RS164-RS169). Outside the band, on admissible models too, the PBH reference agrees with the oracle within 7.3e-15 and the prototype's roots after cancellation within 1.6e-13 (AC5.RS279-RS286, RS292-RS297).
